title: Conducting with a saxophone and learning to conduct
summary: The Cotton Club show writers decide to write Thomas out of the band and make him conductor; he studies conducting and gets a tuxedo.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Then the greatest thing that happened to me at the Cotton Club, them guys who was writing the show, they saw me running out there with my saxophone when Cab would open the show. When he'd go in, I had to go out there and conduct with my saxophone. And the next show, they said, "We're going to write Thomas..." They got together with the big-shots and said, "We're going to write Thomas out of the show and just let him conduct." Because they wanted it to be like a big Broadway show. They didn't want me out there... I looked like a nut out there, directing with the saxophone. I could do it. I went and got me a book, and got in there and studied how to conduct. I got in there and found out... Because I didn't know the first thing you do in conducting through the upbeat... Because it's the only way you can start them right out. You've got to hear the beat when you go up. And I learned how to do the....

Yeah. "And...one, two, three, four, one..." Boy, but these conductors now, they knock me out. They don't knock me out either. But see, they know the works, so they've just got their little things going. And they give the important things, like the upbeat...

Yeah. So that's what gave me a big break, because that... And also, they said, "We're going to buy him a tuxedo..." I've still got that tuxedo. "We're going to buy him a tuxedo and let him get out there and lead the band." So I used to have to go back and change... When the show got ready to play, I used to go back and change into my tuxedo. Because in the beginning, I had to play with the band...
But that was a break for me.
It was a big break for you.
